problem: Compute the sum of the first $12$ terms of the geometric series $1+5+25+⋯$
worked_solution:
Given a geometric series, the sum of the first $N$ terms is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term of the series and $r$ is the common ratio.

In our case, ${a}_{1}=1.$ To find the value of $r,$ we find the ratio of the first two terms in the series:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{5}{1}=5
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=1,N=12$ and $r=5$ into our formula, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{12} & =1\cdot \frac{1-{5}^{12}}{1-5} \\  & =\frac{1-{5}^{12}}{-4} \\  & =\frac{-244\,140\,624}{-4} \\  & =61\,035\,156\end{aligned}
$$
